title: Maximum in Each K-Length Window
statement: A conveyor belt carries readings past a viewing slot exactly k units wide. Given an integer list nums and an integer k with 1 <= k <= len(nums), slide a window of size k from left to right across nums, one step at a time, and record the maximum value inside the window at each stop. Return these maxima as a list in left-to-right window order. The first window covers indices 0..k-1 and the last covers indices len(nums)-k..len(nums)-1, so the returned list has exactly len(nums) - k + 1 entries. When k == len(nums) there is a single window, so return a one-element list holding the maximum of the whole list.
hints: Recomputing the max of each window from scratch rescans overlapping elements; can you carry useful work from one window to the next instead?
Keep a deque of indices whose values are in decreasing order: the front is always the current window's maximum. Store indices, not values, so you can tell when an element has slid out of the window.

For each new index i: pop indices from the back while their value is <= nums[i], then append i. Expire the front with 'if dq[0] <= i - k: popleft()'. Once i >= k - 1, append nums[dq[0]] as this window's maximum.
